lead: Astronauts have lived on the International Space Station without a break since November 2000. This page lets you live through one day aboard, and works out how fast the station flies, why it slowly sinks, and how the crew stays healthy.
try: Under A day aboard, press Play the day and count the sunrises. Then press Exercise time, and in Air, water and food press No recycling, then Today: 98%.
points: The station flies about 420 km up at about 7.7 km every second, so it goes round Earth in about 93 minutes and the crew sees about 16 sunrises a day.
A tiny bit of air up there slowly drags it down, so every few weeks a cargo ship fires its engines to push it back up.
The crew recycles 98% of its water, and exercises about 2½ hours a day so bones and muscles don't waste away.
